summary: Iteration 9 — frontend real-time polling / cross-device sync fix. Verified AuthContext auto-polls /auth/me every ~10s (topbar balance updated 300->400 automatically within 13s after admin manual credit, with exactly 1 /auth/me call — no infinite loop). Polling correctly STOPS after logout (0 /auth/me calls in 13s post-logout). Wallet Refresh button, transactions list, Withdraw history list, and all three admin pages (Deposits/Withdrawals/Support) have working refresh buttons + count in heading. Admin auto-refresh proven: new user deposit made count go 4->5 within 12s; new user support ticket made count go 4->5 within 14s.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.jsx: setInterval is created inside a useEffect gated on [user, refresh]. Because refresh is a useCallback with [] deps it is stable, and user changes from null->object once at login, so the interval is created once — good. Confirmed no duplicate intervals via runtime measurement (1 call / 10s).

AuthContext.jsx: On tab focus the code calls refresh(); if the user rapidly focuses/blurs (e.g., alt-tabbing), each focus fires an /auth/me. Consider debouncing focus/visibility handlers to avoid burst requests. Non-blocking.

rca of the issue: Original bug: same user showed different balances across devices because pages read AuthContext.user once at mount and never refetched. Fix (verified working): AuthProvider now polls GET /auth/me every 10s while user is truthy, plus on window focus and document visibilitychange. Because topbar-balance renders user.balance from context, the DOM refreshes automatically. Reproduction test in this iteration: logged in Playwright as testuser, called admin manual credit API from same page context, waited 13s without any UI action — balance went 300->400 with only 1 /auth/me call. Logout cleanup verified via useEffect return unmounting the interval + event listeners (0 calls in 13s post-logout).
